newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks open financial system after Thai crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks open financial system after Thai crisis.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury, exonerating speculators from blame for Thailand's currency crisis, said on Tuesday that problems there highlighted the need for an open world financial system.

Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, in remarks prepared for delivery to a congressional group, said the United States was committed to liberalizing financial services -- allowing companies easy access to markets outside their home country.
"Recent events in Southeast Asia have only increased our desire to work to strengthen the world's financial systems -- and make them more open," Summers said.

"We believe these to be complementary, not conflicting, goals and we will go the extra mile to convince doubtful emerging economies this is the case... We will be looking for them to commit themselves to substantially full market access and national treatment for financial service providers."
Summers said that Thailand's "unsustainable macroeconomic policy mix" was one factor leading to thelation which forced the country to devalue the baht currency.

Thailand won a $16 billion international loan bailout on Monday. Some critics in the region have said that a relatively open Thai economy meant Thailand was attracting speculators, but Summers said that was not the case. "Blaming foreign speculators for serious economic problems...is rarely, if ever, justified," he said.
